Alright, the recent changes I've made revolve around enabling a headless verification mode that renders the scene without the UI menu, and also positioning the camera at the player's spawn location so the screenshot reflects an in‑game view rather than just the HUD overlay. 

First, I edited `world.js` to hide the `solids` group (raycast‑only meshes) and tweaked a waypoint set to bring the player into a more central area. Then I adjusted the player's initial yaw to face the opposite direction (`-Math.PI / 2`) both in the spawn config and the reset logic, ensuring the player looks toward the intended scene. After confirming the build succeeded, I launched the dev server and verified it responded with a 200 status.

Next, I attempted a headless screenshot using Edge, but the binary wasn't found, so I fell back to Chrome. The first screenshot (`fps_check.png`) captured the default page with the menu overlay; that was expected because the hash was not set. I then added a conditional block in `main.js` that, when the URL hash is `#screenshot`, hides the menu, shows the HUD, and calls `updateHUD()`. The second screenshot (`fps_check2.png`) confirmed that the UI overlay was hidden and the HUD was visible, but the camera was still at its default position (likely the default orbit camera), not from the player's perspective.

To truly verify that the player spawns correctly and the scene renders as intended, I need the camera to be placed at the player's spawn location and oriented according to the player's yaw. I updated the conditional block to set `camera.position` to the player's position (`player.pos.x`, `player.pos.y + player.eyeHeight`, `player.pos.z`) and `camera.rotation` to match the player's yaw (`0, player.yaw, 0` in 'YXZ' order). This ensures that when the `#screenshot` hash is present, the rendered view will be from the player's eyes.

Now that the code is in place, the next logical step is to actually capture a screenshot under this new configuration to confirm that the camera is correctly positioned at the spawn point and that the HUD is rendered without the menu. I will invoke Chrome in headless mode again, targeting the same `#screenshot` hash, and save the output to a new temporary file (`fps_check3.png`). Using a distinct filename avoids any confusion with the previous screenshots and lets me compare the results. The command will mirror the earlier successful screenshot command, just with a different output path.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is a PowerShell command that runs Chrome headlessly, takes a screenshot of `http://localhost:5173/#screenshot`, saves it to `%TEMP%\fps_check3.png`, waits a second, and then checks that the file exists. This will give me concrete evidence that the player’s spawn viewpoint is rendered correctly.
